text:
I read all 10 tracked files. The findings below are ordered by impact. `geo.config.json` sets the intended policy: allow AI search crawlers, block training crawlers. ## High impact 1. **Pricing page is `noindex` but listed in the sitemap.** - `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` sets `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`, and `public/sitemap.xml:4` lists `/pricing`. - The page is the one buyers and AI assistants most often need for "how much does Ledger cost?". `noindex` removes it from search results and AI answers, and the sitemap entry contradicts it. - Fix: remove `robots: { index: false ... }` from the metadata. 2. **Blog content is client-rendered, so crawlers see an empty page.** - `app/blog/page.tsx:1` is a `'use client'` component that fills `posts` in `useEffect` with `fetch('/api/posts')` (lines 7–9). - Most AI crawlers and many search bots don't run JS, so they see `

Blog

` and nothing else. - There is also no `app/api/posts` route in the repo, so the fetch may 404. - Fix: make it a server component and load the posts at render time. - Also add `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` so each post has its own URL, and add those URLs to the sitemap. Currently `public/sitemap.xml` only has the 4 top-level pages. - A client component can't export `metadata`, which is why this page has no title or description of its own. The server-component fix resolves that too. 3. **`robots.txt` doesn't implement your training-block policy.** - `public/robots.txt:4-5` blocks only `GPTBot`, while `geo.config.json:8` says all training crawlers should be blocked. - Fix: add `Disallow: /` groups for `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Bytespider` and `meta-externalagent`. - Leave `OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `PerplexityBot`, `Claude-SearchBot` and `Claude-User` allowed. The `User-agent: *` / `Allow: /` group already covers them. Don't add a blanket block that catches them. - Add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml`, which is missing. ## Medium impact 4. **`` has no `lang`.** `app/layout.tsx:11` should be ``, matching `geo.config.json:4`. 5. **No structured data anywhere.** - Add `Organization` and `WebSite` JSON-LD in `app/layout.tsx`. - Add `Product` or `SoftwareApplication` with offers on the pricing page. - Add `Article` on blog posts. 6. **Thin, near-identical metadata.** - `app/docs/page.tsx:1` has the title "Docs" and `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` has "Pricing". Neither says what the product is. - Use something like "Ledger Docs: set up bank feeds" and "Ledger Pricing: free for up to 3 people". - `app/layout.tsx:6` and `app/page.tsx:1` use the same generic description. Write a distinct, specific description for each page. 7. **Canonical and social tags are missing.** - `app/docs/page.tsx` and `app/blog/page.tsx` have no `alternates.canonical`, and `app/thank-you/page.tsx` has none either. - The layout has no default `openGraph` or `twitter` metadata (`app/layout.tsx:3-7`). - Set a default `alternates.canonical` in the layout, or use per-page canonicals as the home and pricing pages do. 8. **Page content is too thin to be cited.** - Each page is a heading plus one sentence (`app/page.tsx:4`, `app/docs/page.tsx:4`, `app/pricing/page.tsx:4`). - AI engines need substantive text: features, plan tiers and limits, an FAQ, and real docs steps. Use headings and tables that can be quoted directly. ## Low impact 9. **Sitemap is static and has no ``** (`public/sitemap.xml`). Generate it with `app/sitemap.ts` so blog posts are included automatically and carry dates. 10. **Nav uses plain `` tags** (`app/layout.tsx:13`). `next/link` gives client-side navigation and prefetching. Crawlers follow either one, so this isn't an SEO blocker. 11. **Optional:** add `public/llms.txt` with a short site summary and links to the key pages (pricing, docs). ## What's fine - `thank-you` is correctly `noindex` and absent from the sitemap. - `metadataBase` is set (`app/layout.tsx:4`). - Home has a canonical. - The cookie notice's `data-nosnippet` (`app/layout.tsx:15`) is harmless. I haven't changed anything. I can apply fixes 1–5 now if you'd like.
